transcript.text: indesit oven stoped heating, fan goes round n light on but its stone cold after 20 mins. grill werks fine tho. any ideas b4 i call some1 out

The fan running but no heat while the grill works points to a failed fan oven element. It's the most common fault on Indesits, and it's usually a cheap, fairly easy fix.

## Quick checks first
1. Try conventional/top & bottom heat (if your oven has it). If that heats but fan mode doesn't, it's almost certainly the fan element.
2. Check the clock/timer. On many Indesits, if the clock is flashing or stuck in auto mode (e.g. after a power cut), the oven won't heat. Set the time and press the manual (hand symbol) button.
3. Look at the element. It's the circular one behind the back panel inside the oven. Signs of failure include visible breaks, blistering, or scorch marks.

## Likely culprits (most to least likely)
• Fan oven element: About £15–30 for a replacement
• Thermal cut-out: Can trip on just the oven circuit
• Burnt wire or terminal at the element connections
• Thermostat or selector switch: Less common

## If you want to DIY the element
1. Turn off the power at the cooker isolator or fuse box, not just the knob.
2. Unscrew the back panel inside the oven, usually 4 screws.
3. Undo the 2 screws holding the element and pull it forward gently.
4. Disconnect the 2 terminals and take a photo first.
5. Test it with a multimeter if you have one. A working element reads roughly 20–40 ohms. No reading means it's dead.
6. Fit the new one and reassemble.

Get your model number from the sticker on the door frame or the edge of the oven before ordering parts. Elements vary between models.

If the element tests fine, or you're not comfortable with it, that's when to call someone out. At least you'll be able to tell them what you've already ruled out.

clock is set n its in manual, nothing flashing. not sure if mine has a conventional setting tbh. isolated it at the wall cooker switch n took the back panel off, theres a blister/split in the element coil near the bottom with a black mark. no multimeter tho. is that the element dead then?

Yes, that's your culprit. A split or blister with a black scorch mark means the element has burnt out. You don't need a multimeter to confirm that one; it's visibly broken.

## Ordering the right part
• Get the model number from the sticker. It's usually on the oven frame when you open the door, sometimes on the side or underneath the drawer. Write down the full model and serial/code line, as Indesit has many variants.
• Search "[model number] fan oven element". Genuine or decent compatible ones are typically £15–30.
• Match it to your old one: same wattage (often around 2000–2500W, stamped on the element tag), same shape, and same screw hole and terminal positions.

## While you've got it apart
When you undo the element and pull it forward, check the two wire connectors on the back:
• If they're clean and tight, you're good.
• If they're brown, melted, or crumbly, the connectors or wire ends will need replacing too. A burnt terminal can kill a new element quickly.

## Fitting tips
• Keep it isolated at the wall switch the whole time.
• Take a photo of the wiring before disconnecting. Usually it doesn't matter which wire goes on which terminal, but it's reassuring.
• Push the connectors on firmly. Loose ones overheat.
• Make sure the element doesn't touch the fan blade. Spin the fan by hand before refitting the back panel.

## First use
Run it empty at around 200°C for 15–20 minutes. A bit of smoke or a burning smell is normal as the coating burns off a new element. Open a window.

If the new element's fitted and it still won't heat, the next suspect would be the thermal cut-out. But given what you've found, I'd be surprised if it's anything other than the element. Nice bit of diagnosing.
